brief: A MURMURATION at dusk. The roofline and the sky over the river are the top third of every wide shot, and apart from chimney smoke and two vanes nothing moves up there; nothing in the town flocks. In autumn and winter (from the first shed day, leafShed() > 0.1, through midwinter to the first leafOut — read seasonPhase/leafShed/leafOut, do not invent a calendar), on a dry evening (not raining, windF < 0.7), a flock of starlings gathers over the river and far bank in the last stretch of daylight — time-compressed to ~1.2 h sim (~2.7 real s; a twenty-minute one would be 0.75 s and nobody would see it): forming from sunDown − 1.3 h, boiling and turning against the sky as one soft cloud (a particle FIELD of 80–160 dots with two or three drifting attractors and a per-particle hash phase — NOT birds[] agents), leaning downwind off windDir(), then funnelling down into a roost at sunDown − 0.1: the church tower and the far-bank ridges (CHURCH; the eyot's willow may take a share). At sunrise a thin skein leaves the roost. Draw it as ONE live pass between drawBackdrop and the roof rows so it passes BEHIND the spire and the clock tower, and let applyLight/nightF own its colour (it is dark against a bright sky, then gone). No R(): hash(day, k) for the day's flock size, hashes for phases — zero reshuffle, canvas IDENTICAL to HEAD with the season forced to summer. nameAt over the cloud: 'starlings coming in to roost'; one announce as it forms; the evening lapse (sunDown + 1) passes through it — the filmstrip of that lapse must show the cloud and must not POP when it dissolves into the roost (fade the roost's last particles over ≥ 0.3 s real).
successLooksLike: probes/murmur.mjs, 8 seeds × 26 days: forms on ≥ 60% of dry autumn/winter evenings, 0 in summer, 0 in rain; canvas hash IDENTICAL to HEAD with the season forced to summer over the run (the identity law); frame-cost ≤ +0.5 ms at 160 particles; shots/b96-murmur-*.png at sunDown − 0.8 (wide) and in the Far bank quarter show a legible cloud, not a smear; the evening-lapse filmstrip shows it and grades 0 POP at the roost; nameAt reads under the pointer.
avoid: Not birds[] agents and not a per-bird R(). Do not touch the belfry pigeons' bell 'wheel' or belfryRoost. Not filed under Sky (sky × polish is saturated; this is the roofline's first new thing). No new OFFERS entry.
